hypothesis: Monotonic exact-integer deadline arithmetic and aggregate acknowledgements eliminate wall-clock extension, timeout conversion overflow and misleading cleanup completion reports.
scope: Six sequential runServeShutdown cleanup stages; no worker-registry, route admission, position ownership or order authority change.
verification: Pinned Z3 integer obligations, finite six-stage model, source-bound compiled Haskell differential and failure tests, canonical formal/full CI.
failureConditions: deadline expired but new cleanup dispatched
failed step reported as all acknowledged
assumptions: terminating monotonic clock and bounded scheduler service
no monotonic clock wrap during one shutdown
bounded logging and OS primitives for any wall-time interpretation
limitations: Timeouts bound waiting conditionally, not termination of uninterruptible child actions. No full runtime refinement or global shutdown/drain closure. Existing evidence and v1 policies remain frozen.
